answer: One defense is graduated onboarding with time-locked trust. A new agent cannot forge a credible history overnight: it starts with a tiny transaction cap, and each increase requires a voyage of sustained, attested useful work over weeks. Raising the cap is slow and public, so an attacker who wants a thousand Sybils must fund and maintain a thousand visible, time-consuming histories. A single identity is as light as a zephyr to create, but a fleet of trusted ones is expensive to grow and easy to spot.
